definition_zh: 溢出；洒出；泄漏；倾泻；泄露（消息）；（名）洒出的量
definition_en: to flow over the edge of a container accidentally, or to let a secret out
core_image: 杯口一斜，液体越过边缘流得到处都是
scene: 餐桌一角的水杯被袖子带歪了。 Soup spilled onto the cloth as the waiter rushed over.
sceneCN: 这里 spill 是「洒出、溢出」（第 1 个义项：液体意外流出容器）；句意为汤洒到了桌布上。图中可辨识物件：餐桌、汤碗、桌布。

pos.zh: 及物动词：使洒出；使溢出

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词化后缀构成，义为「溢出效应；外溢影响」
英式过去分词形式，义为「洒出的」

senses.title: To flow over the edge accidentally
senses.definition: to flow or fall out of a container over its edge by accident
senses.definitionCN: 液体或物品因意外越过容器边缘流出或落下
senses.example: Milk spilled across the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶洒满了厨房地板。
senses.why: The tilted cup opens an unplanned path: what was held escapes its edge.
senses.whyCN: 倾斜的杯子开出一条计划外的路径：所持之物越过边缘逃走。

senses.title: To make a liquid overflow
senses.definition: to cause a liquid or contents to overflow from a container
senses.definitionCN: 使液体或内容物从容器中溢出
senses.example: He spilled coffee all over the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 他把咖啡洒了满键盘。
senses.why: A hand, not chance, tips the cup this time.
senses.whyCN: 这次是手，不是运气，把杯子弄翻。

senses.title: To pour out in a flood
senses.definition: to pour out, flow out, or spread in large numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 大量地流出、涌出或散开
senses.example: Crowds spilled out of the stadium gates.
senses.exampleCN: 人群从体育场大门涌出。
senses.why: The edge cannot hold what surges: people and light pour like liquid.
senses.whyCN: 边缘盛不下涌动之物：人群和光像液体一样倾泻。

senses.title: To reveal a secret
senses.definition: to let information escape from where it was kept, as in spill the beans
senses.definitionCN: 让消息从保存之处泄露，如 spill the beans
senses.example: One of the clerks finally spilled the secret to the press.
senses.exampleCN: 一名职员最终向媒体说漏了秘密。
senses.why: Information is treated like liquid in a jar: one tip and it runs.
senses.whyCN: 信息被当作罐中液体：一倾斜就流走。

senses.title: To scatter from a moving container
senses.definition: to scatter or fall out of a moving vehicle or holder
senses.definitionCN: 从行进的车辆或承载物中散落
senses.example: The truck spilled gravel across the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在转弯处撒了一路碎石。
senses.why: A moving edge shakes loose whatever it no longer grips.
senses.whyCN: 行进的边缘抖落一切它握不住的东西。

senses.title: A fall or tumble
senses.definition: a sudden fall from a bicycle, horse, or height
senses.definitionCN: 从自行车、马背或高处突然跌落
senses.example: The rider took a nasty spill on the gravel path.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手在碎石路上重重摔了一跤。
senses.why: What escapes the edge may be the rider: bodies spill as liquids do.
senses.whyCN: 越过边缘的可能是骑手：身体如液体般洒落。

senses.title: The amount that overflows
senses.definition: the amount of liquid or material that has overflowed
senses.definitionCN: 溢出的液体或材料量
senses.example: The crew cleaned an oil spill near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 船员清理了海岸附近的一次漏油。
senses.why: The escaped liquid becomes a thing itself, measured and mourned.
senses.whyCN: 逃逸的液体自成一物，被计量、被哀悼。

senses.title: To spill over into neighbouring areas
senses.definition: to extend beyond one place or situation and affect others, as in spill over
senses.definitionCN: 越过一处范围影响他处，如 spill over
senses.example: The border conflict spilled over into neighbouring districts.
senses.exampleCN: 边境冲突波及了邻近地区。
senses.why: Trouble ignores boundaries: it flows wherever the land tilts.
senses.whyCN: 麻烦无视边界：土地向哪里倾斜，它就流向哪里。

intro.en: Spill is a native English word whose old meaning was to destroy, before liquids took over the word.
intro.cn: spill 是本土英语词，其古老意义是「毁灭」，后来才被「液体」占用了这个词。

items.en: *spilthan- is generally reconstructed for "to destroy, kill"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始日耳曼语 *spilthan- 表示「毁灭、杀」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English spillan meant "to destroy, ruin, kill"; blood was spilled in battle in the old sense.
items.cn: 古英语 spillan 意为「毁灭、毁坏、杀」；旧义中「流血洒地」即出自此。

items.en: In Middle English the sense narrowed to letting liquids or grain escape a container.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，词义收窄为让液体或谷物从容器流失。

items.en: English kept both spilled and spilt, the -t form stronger in British usage.
items.cn: 英语同时保留 spilled 与 spilt 两种形式，-t 形式在英式用法中更强。

items.en: The word now covers liquids, crowds, secrets, oil and even stock-market spillover.
items.cn: 现代英语中，该词涵盖液体、人群、秘密、石油乃至股市外溢。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the native family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of overflowing and leaking.
note.cn: 形近组收本土词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示溢出与泄漏的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for effects that spread beyond their first place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指超出原地的外溢影响。

entries.definition: British past form of spill, also used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: spill 的英式过去形式，也作形容词。

entries.definition: A channel that lets excess water escape a dam.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指让水库多余水泄出的溢洪道。

entries.definition: Quiet or continuing; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「静止的、仍然」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sharp point or sudden rise; one letter apart and of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「尖刺、骤增」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: To flow beyond the brim; overlaps the liquid sense.
entries.definitionCN: 越过边缘流出，与液体义项重叠。

entries.definition: To escape through a hole, of liquids or secrets.
entries.definitionCN: 液体或秘密经孔洞逸出。

entries.definition: To flow in a stream, deliberately or heavily.
entries.definitionCN: 成流涌出，或有意或倾盆。

entries.definition: To let fall or lose naturally, as leaves or tears.
entries.definitionCN: 自然落下或失去，如落叶、落泪。

entries.definition: To spread widely in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: 向不同方向散开。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real old sense and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古义，以及该词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Spill the beans is the famous idiom for telling secrets.
normal.cn: spill the beans 是「说漏嘴」的著名习语。

normal.en: The old sense was destroy: spill blood once meant kill.
normal.cn: 古义是毁灭：spill blood 曾指杀戮。

normal.en: Spill over means trouble flows past its border.
normal.cn: spill over 表示麻烦流过边界。

normal.en: Oil spill names one of the worst accidents at sea.
normal.cn: oil spill 指海上最严重的事故之一。

normal.en: British English often uses spilt as the past form.
normal.cn: 英式英语常用 spilt 作过去式。

abstract.en: Picture every edge in the world as a brim waiting for one tilt.
abstract.cn: 想象世上每条边缘都是一道杯沿，等待一次倾斜。

abstract.en: Secrets behave like ink: once spilled, no cloth restores the page.
abstract.cn: 秘密像墨水：一旦洒出，任何布都无法复原纸页。

abstract.en: A crowd held too long behind gates spills the moment they open.
abstract.cn: 在闸门后憋得太久的人群，开门一刻便涌出。

examples.en: She spilled juice on the report this morning.
examples.cn: 她今早把果汁洒在了报告上。

examples.en: Light spilled from every window of the tall building.
examples.cn: 高楼每扇窗都透出灯光。

examples.en: The oil spill damaged hundreds of kilometres of coastline.
examples.cn: 漏油事故破坏了数百公里海岸线。

root: spill 属日耳曼语本土词：古英语 spillan「毁灭、毁坏」，一般认为源于原始日耳曼语 *spilthan-「毁灭」，更早来源不确定；中古英语起词义收窄为「溢出、洒出」，古老的「流血毁灭」义仍留痕于 spill blood。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of spill all cross an edge: liquids over brims, crowds past gates, secrets out of jars, and trouble past borders.
sensesIntro.cn: spill 的各项义项都在跨越一条边缘：液体越过杯沿、人群涌过闸门、秘密溜出罐口、麻烦漫过边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tilted cup whose brim can no longer hold what it carries.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倾斜的杯子，边缘再也盛不住所载之物。

branches.en: THE LIQUID LINE: what escapes is measured, cleaned, or mourned.
branches.cn: 液体线：逃逸之物被计量、清理或哀悼。

branches.en: THE FLOOD LINE: crowds, light and gravel pour like liquid over edges.
branches.cn: 倾泻线：人群、光与碎石如液体般越过边缘。

branches.en: THE SECRET LINE: information tips out of its jar with one careless move.
branches.cn: 泄密线：信息一次不慎便从罐中倾出。

branches.en: THE FALL LINE: bodies spill too, from saddles and bicycles.
branches.cn: 跌落线：身体也会洒落，从马背与自行车上。

branches.en: THE BORDER LINE: trouble spills over into the next valley and the next market.
branches.cn: 边界线：麻烦漫入下一座山谷与下一个市场。

intro.en: Spill is a bare native root; English compounds grow beside it rather than on it.
intro.cn: spill 是本土裸词根；英语的复合词长在它旁边而非其上。

definition_zh: 可供选择的方案；替代品；可供选择的；非传统的；另类的
definition_en: one of two or more possible choices, something used in place of another, or an adjective describing an option outside the usual course
core_image: 岔路口立着两块路牌，一块是常走的路，另一块是另一条
scene: 会议桌上摊着两份预算，一份保守，一份激进。 The board rejected the first plan and asked for an alternative.
sceneCN: 这里 alternative 是「替代方案」（第 2 个义项：可以顶替原有做法的事物）；句意为董事会否决了第一份方案，要求另提一个方案。画面里是摊开的预算表与两支笔。

pos.zh: 名词：可供选择的方案；替代品；备选项
形容词：可供选择的；替代的；非传统的；另类的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「或者；作为另一种选择」
由同一拉丁词根 alternare 构成，义为「交替、轮流」，作形容词时义为「间隔的」
由 alternare 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「交替、轮换」
由 alternare 加表施动者的后缀 -or 构成，义为「交流发电机」

senses.title: One of two or more possible choices
senses.definition: one of the things you can choose between when a decision has to be made
senses.definitionCN: 必须作出决定时，可供你在其中挑选的若干事物之一
senses.example: We weighed two alternatives for a week before signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 签约前我们用了一周时间权衡两个方案。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin alter, the other of two, so the noun names the other item lying on the table beside the first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」之上，所以名词指的就是摆在第一个选项旁边的那「另一个」，即选项之一。

senses.title: A thing used instead of another
senses.definition: something that can take the place of the thing normally used
senses.definitionCN: 能够占据平时所用之物位置的东西
senses.example: For many commuters the bicycle is a cheap alternative to the car.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多通勤者来说，自行车是汽车的廉价替代品。
senses.why: Once an item is the other one of the pair, it can occupy the first one's place, and substitution is that pairing image put into action.
senses.whyCN: 一项东西既然是成对里的「另一个」，就能占据第一个的位置；替代义正是把「成对」的画面变成实际行动。

senses.title: Another possibility offered as a choice
senses.definition: used about a plan, route or method that can be chosen instead of the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述可以代替常规做法被选中的计划、路线或方法
senses.example: The airline put us on an alternative flight the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司把我们安排到了第二天早上的另一趟航班。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply marks the second item before the noun and leaves the choosing to the reader.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是把「第二个」这个身份贴到名词前面，把选择留给读者去做，所以译作「备选的」。

senses.title: Outside the mainstream
senses.definition: describing a treatment, energy source or way of living that differs from the conventional one
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同于常规做法的疗法、能源或生活方式
senses.example: The clinic is known for alternative treatments that avoid strong drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所以不用强效药物的另类疗法闻名。
senses.why: Once the pair becomes mainstream versus other, the second item stops being neutral and takes on the colour of dissent.
senses.whyCN: 当这对选项变成「主流与另一个」时，第二个就不再中性，而带上了不从众的色彩，于是成了「非传统」的标签。

senses.title: No alternative but to
senses.definition: in the phrase have no alternative but to, to be forced into one course because nothing else is open
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 have no alternative but to，表示因别无他路而被迫走某一条路
senses.example: With the bridge closed, drivers had no alternative but to take the long road.
senses.exampleCN: 桥封了，司机们别无选择，只能绕远路。
senses.why: The pair collapses into a single option: when the other one does not exist, what remains is not really a choice at all.
senses.whyCN: 成对的选项塌缩成一个：当「另一个」根本不存在时，剩下的那条路其实算不上选择，于是这个短语表示「只能如此」。

intro.en: Alternative is the Latin alter family again, this time carried through a verb and an adjective ending.
intro.cn: alternative 仍是拉丁语 alter 一族，只是这回经过一个动词和一个形容词词尾。

items.en: Alter meant the other of two and is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: Alter plus an adjective ending gave alternus, one after the other or alternate.
items.cn: alter 加形容词词尾构成 alternus，意为「轮流、交替的」。

items.en: The verb alternare meant to do by turns; English alternate comes from the same verb.
items.cn: 动词 alternare 意为「轮流、交替做」，英语 alternate 出自同一个动词。

items.en: Medieval Latin alternativus, forming a choice between two, passed through French alternatif into English.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alternativus 意为「构成二选一的」，经法语 alternatif 进入英语。

items.en: The noun sense one of two courses is recorded from the seventeenth century, while the unconventional sense belongs to the twentieth; exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 名词义「两条路中的一条」自十七世纪有记录，「非传统」义则属于二十世纪；确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Latin alternus root; the near-meaning group holds words for choices and stand-ins.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语 alternus 词根构成的词；近义组收表示「选择」与「顶替」的词。

entries.definition: To take turns, or an adjective for every other one in a series.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交替、轮流」；作形容词时义为「间隔的、隔一个的」。

entries.definition: In turns, one after the other.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「交替地、轮流地」，由 alternate 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of taking turns or changing repeatedly between two states.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交替、轮换」，指在两种状态之间反复更换。

entries.definition: A machine that produces alternating current.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交流发电机」，指产生交变电流的机器。

entries.definition: As another possibility; used to introduce a second option in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「或者、作为另一种选择」，在书面语中引出第二个选项。

entries.definition: A thing that may be chosen; neutral in tone and common in business and law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选项、选择权」，语气中性，常见于商务与法律语境。

entries.definition: The range of things to choose from, or the act of choosing; broader than alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选择、可供选择的范围」，范围比 alternative 更宽。

entries.definition: A person or thing that takes the place of another, often with no sense of choice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替代者、代替物」，通常不带「可供选择」的意味。

entries.definition: A reserve option kept ready in case the first one fails.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后备、备用方案」，指为防第一个失效而预留的选择。

entries.definition: Something that fills the place of a thing that has gone or been used up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替换物」，指填补已消失或用尽之物位置的东西。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin alter base and the real phrases the word forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用 alter 这个拉丁语词基，以及这个词真实构成的搭配。

normal.en: Alter is the other of two, so an alternative is that other one offered as a choice.
normal.cn: alter 是「两者中的另一个」，所以 alternative 就是被摆出来供人挑选的那「另一个」。

normal.en: The ending -ive keeps the word adjectival, so it can stand before a noun: an alternative plan.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 让它保持形容词性质，可以放在名词前：an alternative plan。

normal.en: Have no alternative but to marks the moment the pair of options shrinks to one.
normal.cn: have no alternative but to 标记的正是成对选项缩成一个的时刻。

normal.en: Alternative medicine is simply the other route beside mainstream medicine.
normal.cn: alternative medicine 不过是主流医学旁边的另一条路。

normal.en: Alternative and alternate differ by one ending: a choice versus taking turns.
normal.cn: alternative 与 alternate 只差一个词尾：一个是可选项，一个是轮流。

abstract.en: Picture two signposts at a fork: one points to the usual road, the other is blank until you name it.
abstract.cn: 想象岔路口的两块路牌：一块指向常走的路，另一块在你给它命名之前是空白的。

abstract.en: The blank sign is not a worse road, only a road you have not taken yet.
abstract.cn: 那块空白路牌并不代表更差的路，只是一条你还没走过的路。

abstract.en: When the usual sign falls down, the blank one is all that is left, which is why the word also means the only way out.
abstract.cn: 当常走的那块牌子倒下，空白的这块就成了唯一剩下的一条，这正是该词也表「唯一出路」的原因。

examples.en: Cycling is a healthy alternative to driving for short trips.
examples.cn: 短途出行时，骑车是比开车更健康的替代方式。

examples.en: The committee could see no alternative to closing the library on Sundays.
examples.cn: 委员会看不出除了周日关闭图书馆之外还有别的办法。

examples.en: She avoids sugar and uses honey as an alternative sweetener.
examples.cn: 她不吃糖，改用蜂蜜作为替代甜味剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥特纳提夫」——奥特曼站在岔路口，总得挑另一个方案：替代方案

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」加形容词词尾构成 alternus「交替的」，再加动词词尾 -are 成 alternare「轮流做」；中世纪拉丁语 alternativus「构成二选一的」经法语 alternatif 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of alternative all come from the paired option: a possible choice, a stand-in, an available second option, a route outside the mainstream, and the phrase for having no other route at all.
sensesIntro.cn: alternative 的五个义项都来自「成对的选项」：可选项、替代品、备选项、主流之外的路线，以及表示再无他路可走的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signposts stand at a fork, one for the usual road and one for its other.
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口立着两块路牌，一块指向常走的路，一块指向它的另一条。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: the second signpost is simply one of the things you may pick.
branches.cn: 选择线：第二块路牌只是你可以挑选的事物之一。

branches.en: THE STAND-IN: the second thing can take the first one's place.
branches.cn: 替换线：第二个东西可以占据第一个的位置。

branches.en: THE LABEL: placed before a noun, the word marks an option rather than naming one.
branches.cn: 标签线：放在名词前时，这个词只标记「备选」，而不指认具体某一条。

branches.en: THE DISSENT: once the pair is mainstream versus other, the other side carries a flavour of refusal.
branches.cn: 异见线：一旦这对变成「主流与另一个」，另一侧就带上了拒斥常规的意味。

branches.en: THE DEAD END: with the other signpost gone, the word turns into the phrase for having no choice.
branches.cn: 绝路线：另一块路牌不在了，这个词就转为表示「别无选择」的说法。

intro.en: Alternative is built from the Latin base alter plus a verb ending and an adjective suffix; English adds ordinary endings to grow the family.
intro.cn: alternative 由拉丁语词基 alter 加动词词尾和形容词后缀构成；英语再用普通词尾扩展这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alter, alternus, alternare and alternativus are all recorded, so only the Indo-European root behind alter is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alter、alternus、alternare、alternativus 都有文献记录，只有 alter 背后的印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The base supplies the idea of a paired option.
items.exampleCN: 这个词基提供「成对选项」的意思。

definition_zh: 具体指定；明确说明；详细列明
definition_en: to state something exactly and clearly, naming the details or requirements
core_image: 在图纸空白处逐项写清要求：一条一条，不留悬念
scene: 装修的草图摊在桌上，客户逐行签字确认。 The client asked the builder to specify every material in the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 specify 是「明确说明、详细列明」（第 1 个义项：确切而清楚地陈述）；句意为客户要求施工方在合同中列明每一种材料。图中可辨识物件：草图、笔、合同文本。

pos.zh: 动词：具体指定；明确说明；详细列明

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「规格；说明书；明确说明」
同族形容词，义为「明确的；特定的」
同族副词，义为「明确地；特意地」
由同族形容词加后缀构成，义为「明确性；特异性」

senses.title: To state exactly and clearly
senses.definition: to say or write something in a precise, unmistakable form
senses.definitionCN: 以精确、不含糊的形式说出或写下
senses.example: The contract specifies the delivery date in bold letters.
senses.exampleCN: 合同以粗体字写明交货日期。
senses.why: The pen writes one line per requirement: nothing is left to guess.
senses.whyCN: 笔为每条要求各写一行：不留下任何猜测。

senses.title: To name the very thing required
senses.definition: to identify the exact thing wanted rather than a general class
senses.definitionCN: 指明确切所需之物，而非笼统一类
senses.example: The recipe specifies unsalted butter, not any butter.
senses.exampleCN: 食谱指定无盐黄油，而不是任何黄油。
senses.why: Naming beats describing: the pointed finger touches one object only.
senses.whyCN: 指名胜于描述：手指只触到一个对象。

senses.title: To set out requirements item by item
senses.definition: to list conditions, measurements, or parts one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把条件、尺寸或部件逐条列出
senses.example: The engineer specified each bolt size for the frame.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师逐条列明框架的每个螺栓尺寸。
senses.why: The list grows line by line until the whole design is pinned down.
senses.whyCN: 清单逐行增长，直至整个设计被钉牢。

senses.title: To fix a time or amount
senses.definition: to settle an exact date, time, or quantity in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先确定确切的日期、时间或数量
senses.example: The invitation specified half past seven, not later.
senses.exampleCN: 请柬指定七点半，不得更晚。
senses.why: Numbers and dates are pinned like headings on the written page.
senses.whyCN: 数字与日期像标题一样钉在书面上。

senses.title: In law and contracts: to define terms
senses.definition: to define terms, obligations, or boundaries in a formal document
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文件中界定条款、义务或边界
senses.example: The lease specifies who repairs the heating system.
senses.exampleCN: 租约明确了暖气系统由谁维修。
senses.why: In documents, each line written is a line that cannot be argued later.
senses.whyCN: 在文件中，写下的每一行都是日后无从争辩的一行。

senses.title: In computing and data: to declare parameters
senses.definition: to declare exact parameters, values, or formats in a system or command
senses.definitionCN: 在系统或命令中声明确切的参数、数值或格式
senses.example: The script specifies the output folder and file name.
senses.exampleCN: 脚本指定了输出文件夹和文件名。
senses.why: Machines obey only what is written exactly; vagueness breaks the run.
senses.whyCN: 机器只服从写得确切的东西；含糊会让运行中断。

senses.title: To describe a method precisely
senses.definition: to lay out a procedure or method in exact steps
senses.definitionCN: 以确切步骤铺陈程序或方法
senses.example: The lab manual specifies the order of every reagent added.
senses.exampleCN: 实验手册规定了加入每种试剂的顺序。
senses.why: Steps written in order leave no room for improvisation.
senses.whyCN: 按序写明的步骤不给临场发挥留余地。

senses.title: To make plans definite for others
senses.definition: to fix a plan so that others can act on it without asking
senses.definitionCN: 把计划确定下来，使他人无需再问即可执行
senses.example: The architect specified the exact width of every doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师规定了每个门洞的确切宽度。
senses.why: A plan written precisely travels without its author: the lines speak for him.
senses.whyCN: 写得精确的计划无需作者同行：图纸上的线条替他说话。

intro.en: Specify is the English verb built on the Latin kind-word, made by adding a making-suffix.
intro.cn: specify 是建立在拉丁「种类」词上的英语动词，通过加「做成」后缀构成。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Species meant "a kind, appearance", from specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「种类、外貌」，由 specere「看」派生。

items.en: Medieval Latin specificare meant "to state in terms of a specific kind".
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 specificare 意为「按特定种类来表述」。

items.en: The verb specify appeared in English by the fifteenth to sixteenth century, first in formal writing.
items.cn: 动词 specify 约在十五至十六世纪进入英语，最初用于正式文体。

items.en: Law, engineering and computing made specify the standard verb for exact statement.
items.cn: 法律、工程与计算领域使 specify 成为精确陈述的标准动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same Latin family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of exact statement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示精确陈述的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same family, meaning clear and exact.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词，义为「明确的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the written statement of exact details.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指写明确切细节的文件。

entries.definition: A sample for study; same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To calm someone; merely ends the same way and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「安抚」；只是词尾相同，词源不同。

entries.definition: The adverb of the family, meaning clearly or especially.
entries.definitionCN: 同族副词，义为「明确地；特别地」。

entries.definition: To demand a condition as part of an agreement; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 把条件定为协议的一部分，语气正式。

entries.definition: To list all the parts of something one by one.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物的各部分逐一列出。

entries.definition: To state exactly the meaning or boundaries of something.
entries.definitionCN: 确切陈述某物的含义或边界。

entries.definition: To officially choose and name something for a role.
entries.definitionCN: 正式选定并指名某物承担某一角色。

entries.definition: To name things one by one in a list.
entries.definitionCN: 逐一列举。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real word family and the phrases where the verb appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实词族知识和该动词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: The verb adds -fy, to make, onto specific: to make a statement specific.
normal.cn: 动词在 specific 上加 -fy「使」：使陈述变得具体明确。

normal.en: Unless otherwise specified is the classic contract phrase.
normal.cn: unless otherwise specified 是经典合同用语。

normal.en: Specify what, when, and how much: the verb loves details.
normal.cn: specify 说清是什么、何时、多少：这个动词热爱细节。

normal.en: The same family gives specific, specifically and specification.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 specific、specifically、specification。

normal.en: A specified amount is one written down exactly in advance.
normal.cn: specified amount 指事先确切写明的数额。

abstract.en: Picture a blueprint with every blank already filled: nothing left for the builder to guess.
abstract.cn: 想象一张所有空白都已填好的图纸：施工者无从猜测。

abstract.en: To specify is to trade vagueness for a numbered list.
abstract.cn: specify 就是用一张编号清单换走含糊。

abstract.en: The pen that specifies draws a fence around misunderstanding.
abstract.cn: 用于 specify 的笔在误解周围画下围栏。

examples.en: The form asks you to specify your preferred contact method.
examples.cn: 表格要求你指定首选的联系方式。

examples.en: Safety rules specify that helmets must be worn at all times.
examples.cn: 安全规程明确规定必须始终佩戴头盔。

examples.en: Please specify which version of the software you are using.
examples.cn: 请注明你使用的是哪个版本的软件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西法爱」——白纸黑字一条条写死：具体指定

root: 英语动词 specify 由 specific 加动词后缀 -fy 构成；specific 经晚期拉丁语 specificus 追溯至 species「种类」与 specere「观看」；一般认为印欧词根 *spek- 表示「观察」，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of specify all write the exact thing down: naming, listing, fixing times, defining terms, or declaring parameters.
sensesIntro.cn: specify 的各项义项都在把确切之物写下来：指名、列项、定时、界定条款或声明参数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand filling every blank line of a blueprint so nothing is left to guess.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把图纸上的每条空行都填满，不留下任何猜测。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT LINE: exact words replace vague gestures.
branches.cn: 陈述线：确切的词语取代含糊的手势。

branches.en: THE LIST LINE: item after item, and steps in fixed order.
branches.cn: 清单线：逐项铺陈，步骤按固定顺序。

branches.en: THE FIXING LINE: dates and amounts are pinned in advance.
branches.cn: 定时线：日期与数额事先钉死。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT LINE: written lines in contracts cannot be argued later.
branches.cn: 文件线：合同中写下的行文日后无从争辩。

branches.en: THE MACHINE-AND-PLAN LINE: parameters declared and plans fixed let others act without asking.

definition_zh: 探索；勘探；探究
definition_en: to travel through a place to learn about it; to examine an idea carefully; to search for possibilities
core_image: 走进陌生的地方，一路查看、一路发现
scene: 他们花了一周时间探索这片森林。 They spent a week exploring the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 explore 是「探索」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们花了一周时间探索这片森林。

derivatives.zh: 探索；勘探
探险家
探索性的
探索的

senses.title: Travel to learn
senses.definition: to travel through a place to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 穿行某地以了解它
senses.example: They explored the cave by torchlight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着火把的光探索洞穴。
senses.why: The core sense is searching a new place.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是搜寻新地方。

senses.title: Examine an idea
senses.definition: to examine an idea or subject carefully
senses.definitionCN: 仔细考察一个想法或主题
senses.example: The book explores the causes of war.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书探讨战争的起因。
senses.why: Searching land becomes searching ideas.
senses.whyCN: 搜寻土地变成搜寻想法。

senses.title: Search possibilities
senses.definition: to search for possibilities or choices
senses.definitionCN: 寻找可能性或选择
senses.example: She explored several career options.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究了几种职业选择。
senses.why: Exploring becomes testing what could work.
senses.whyCN: 探索变成试探哪些可行。

intro.en: Explore comes from Latin explorare, to search out.
intro.cn: explore 源自拉丁语 explorare，意为「搜寻出来」。

items.en: Explorare means to search out.
items.cn: explorare 意为搜寻出来。

items.en: It is used for scouting and hunting.
items.cn: 它常用于侦察与狩猎。

items.en: Explorer keeps the sense of scouting.
items.cn: explorer 保留侦察的含义。

items.en: Exploren means to examine a place.
items.cn: exploren 意为考察某地。

items.en: Explore extends to ideas and choices.
items.cn: explore 扩展到想法与选择。

items.en: Explore options is a common phrase.
items.cn: explore options 成为常用搭配。

note.en: Explore is to search and learn; explode is to burst.
note.cn: explore 是探索求知，explode 则是爆炸。

entries.definition: to burst with force

entries.definition: to use or take advantage of

entries.definition: to uncover or make known

entries.definition: to examine facts carefully
entries.definitionCN: 调查

entries.definition: to look at something closely
entries.definitionCN: 检查；审查

entries.definition: to look over a whole area
entries.definitionCN: 勘测；审视

normalIntro.en: Explore is moving through the unknown to find out.
normalIntro.cn: explore 是走进未知去弄个明白。

normal.en: The children explored the woods behind the house.
normal.cn: 孩子们探索了屋后的树林。

normal.en: The report explores why the plan failed.
normal.cn: 报告探究了计划失败的原因。

normal.en: We should explore other ways to save energy.
normal.cn: 我们应当探索其他节能办法。

normal.en: Divers explored the sunken ship.
normal.cn: 潜水员探索了沉船。

normal.en: She explored the city on foot for hours.
normal.cn: 她步行逛了这座城市好几个小时。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp moving through a dark tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯在黑暗隧道中移动。

abstract.en: Imagine a finger tracing a path on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在地图上描出一条路线。

abstract.en: Think of many doors opening one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门依次打开。

examples.en: Scientists continue to explore the deep ocean.
examples.cn: 科学家继续探索深海。

examples.en: The essay explores the meaning of home.
examples.cn: 这篇文章探讨「家」的意义。

examples.en: They explored every option before deciding.
examples.cn: 做决定前他们研究了每一种选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: moving through a strange place to learn.
core.cn: 核心意象：走进陌生之地一路查看。

branches.en: The base sense is searching a new place.
branches.cn: 基础义是搜寻新地方。

branches.en: Physical search becomes study of ideas.
branches.cn: 实地搜寻变成对想法的研究。

branches.en: Searching becomes testing possibilities.

branches.en: Studying ideas and weighing options overlap.
branches.cn: 研究想法与权衡选择相互重叠。

intro.en: Explore comes from Latin explorare, to search out.
intro.cn: explore 来自拉丁语 explorare，意为搜寻出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin explorare supplies the core form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 explorare 提供核心词形。

items.example: Plorare is linked to hunting calls.

definition_zh: 同样地；平等地；均等地
definition_en: in an equal way, or to the same degree
core_image: 两杯水被倒到完全相同的高度
scene: 把奖金平均分给四个孩子。 Divide the prize money equally among the four children.
sceneCN: 这里 equally 是「均等地」（第 1 个义项：以相同的份额或数量）；句意：把奖金平均分给四个孩子。

derivatives.zh: 相等的；同等的人；等于
平等；相等

senses.title: In equal shares
senses.definition: in the same amount or share for each person or part
senses.definitionCN: 给每个人或每一部分相同的数量或份额
senses.example: The money was shared equally between the two sisters.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔钱在两姐妹之间平均分配。
senses.why: The adverb adds -ly to equal, so it describes an action done in an even way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词由 equal 加 -ly 构成，描述以均衡方式完成的动作。

senses.title: To the same degree
senses.definition: to the same degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 达到相同的程度或范围
senses.example: Both plans are equally risky.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案的风险同样大。
senses.why: The balance sense extends from shares to degrees of a quality.
senses.whyCN: 「份额均衡」的概念扩展到某种品质的程度。

senses.title: Used to add a matching point
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to add a point of the same weight
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，补充一个分量相同的观点
senses.example: Equally, we must consider the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 同样，我们也必须考虑成本。
senses.why: If two points weigh the same, the second can be introduced as equally important.
senses.whyCN: 如果两个观点分量相同，第二个就可以作为同样重要的一点引出。

intro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly, from Latin aequalis, even, and aequus, level.
intro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly，来自拉丁语 aequalis（均匀的）与 aequus（平的）。

items.en: Aequus means level or fair.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、公平的。

items.en: Aequalis means even or equal.
items.cn: aequalis 意为均匀的、相等的。

items.en: Equal enters English as an adjective.
items.cn: equal 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ly forms the adverb equally.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 equally。

items.en: Equally also introduces a second point of the same weight.
items.cn: 现代英语中，equally 也用于引出第二个同等分量的观点。

note.en: Equally is the adverb of equal, near its family and near adverbs for sameness.
note.cn: equally 是 equal 的副词，与自身词族以及表示相同的副词相邻。

entries.definition: the same in amount
entries.definitionCN: 相等的

entries.definition: the equal state
entries.definitionCN: 平等；相等

entries.definition: to treat as equal
entries.definitionCN: 等同

entries.definition: in an even or balanced way
entries.definitionCN: 均匀地；平坦地

entries.definition: in the same way
entries.definitionCN: 同样地

entries.definition: in a similar way
entries.definitionCN: 相似地

normalIntro.en: Equally is equal plus -ly: whatever is equal is done or measured in an equal way.
normalIntro.cn: equally 是 equal 加 -ly：相等的东西，就以相等的方式去做或衡量。

normal.en: Divide equally means give everyone the same share.
normal.cn: divide equally 指给每个人相同的一份。

normal.en: Equally important means just as important.
normal.cn: equally important 表示同样重要。

normal.en: Equally spaced dots sit the same distance apart.
normal.cn: equally spaced 的点彼此距离相同。

normal.en: Equally at the start of a sentence adds a matching point.
normal.cn: equally 放在句首，补充一个对等的观点。

normal.en: Compare evenly: evenly stresses smooth distribution, equally stresses sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 evenly：evenly 强调分布平滑，equally 强调相同。

abstract.en: Picture two glasses filled to exactly the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象两只杯子被倒到完全相同的高度。

abstract.en: Imagine a row of trees planted at identical gaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一排树以相同间距种下。

abstract.en: Think of two weights resting level on a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象两个砝码在天平上保持水平。

examples.en: The estate was divided equally among the three children.
examples.cn: 遗产在三个孩子之间平均分配。

examples.en: Both candidates are equally qualified for the job.
examples.cn: 两位候选人都同样胜任这份工作。

examples.en: Equally, we should ask who pays for the repairs.
examples.cn: 同样，我们也应该问清谁来支付维修费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal + ly」——用「相等」的方式去做，就是同样地；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aequus（平的）→ aequalis（相等的）→ 英语 equal ＋ -ly → equally，核心义「以相同的方式或程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Equally starts with equal shares, extends to equal degrees, and is then used to add a point of the same weight.
sensesIntro.cn: equally 从均分开始，扩展到相同程度，随后用于补充同等分量的观点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two containers filled to the same level.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个容器被装到同一高度。

branches.en: Equal shares are the basic distributive sense.
branches.cn: 均分是基本的分配义项。

branches.en: Equal degree extends balance to qualities.
branches.cn: 同等程度把平衡扩展到品质。

branches.en: Adding a matching point uses equal weight in argument.
branches.cn: 补充对等观点，是在论证中使用同等分量。

branches.en: A fair share and an equal degree both rest on the same measure.
branches.cn: 公平份额与相同程度都建立在同一尺度上。

branches.en: Two equally strong points can both be introduced with equally.
branches.cn: 两个同样有力的观点都可以用 equally 引出。

intro.en: Equally is a Latin balance adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aequus 意为平的，aequalis 意为均匀的。

senses.title: To make by sewing

senses.why: The action produces an object.

senses.definitionCN: 用缝线把伤口合起来

normalIntro.en: Sew is the quiet work of a needle pulling thread through cloth.
normalIntro.cn: sew 是针带着线穿过布面的安静工作。

normal.en: She sews her own clothes.

normal.cn: 他在牛仔裤上缝了一块补丁。

definition_zh: 明确的；具体的；特定的；特有的；特效的
definition_en: clearly defined and exact, or relating to one particular thing rather than others
core_image: 放大镜对准一点：众多可能里只锁定那一个
scene: 问卷上的选项太多了，老师指着其中一格。 Please give one specific example from your own experience.
sceneCN: 这里 specific 是「具体的、明确的」（第 1 个义项：清楚确定、不笼统的）；句意为请从你自己的经历中举出一个具体的例子。图中可辨识物件：问卷、铅笔、老师的手。

senses.title: Clearly defined and exact
senses.definition: clear and precise, leaving no doubt about what is meant
senses.definitionCN: 清楚、精确，对所指毫无含糊
senses.example: The report gave a specific date for the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 报告给出了发布的确定日期。
senses.why: The magnifying glass drops on one point: out of many possibilities, one is named exactly.
senses.whyCN: 放大镜落在一点上：在众多可能中，只精确指出一个。

senses.title: Particular rather than general
senses.definition: relating to one particular thing, person, or case rather than things in general
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一特定事物、人或情形，而非泛指
senses.example: This medicine targets a specific type of bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药针对特定的一类细菌。
senses.why: The lens can be aimed: whatever it lands on becomes the special one among many.
senses.whyCN: 镜头可以瞄准：它落到哪里，哪里就从众多中成为被选中的那一个。

senses.title: Peculiar to something
senses.definition: found or effective only in connection with one particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 只与某一特定事物相关或对其有效
senses.example: The rash is specific to this tropical region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种皮疹是这一热带地区特有的。
senses.why: What the lens isolates belongs to that thing alone and to nothing else.
senses.whyCN: 镜头所隔离之物只属于那一事物，不属于其他。

senses.title: Detailed and concrete in information
senses.definition: containing details that are concrete and usable, not vague
senses.definitionCN: 包含具体可用的细节，不含糊其辞
senses.example: Her feedback was specific enough to fix the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反馈足够具体，可以据此修改草稿。
senses.why: Precision has degrees: the more the glass magnifies, the more detail shows.
senses.whyCN: 精确有程度：放大越多，细节越多。

senses.title: In medicine: acting on one target
senses.definition: acting effectively against one particular disease or agent and not others
senses.definitionCN: 只对某一特定疾病或病原有效，对其他无效
senses.example: Quinine became a specific treatment for malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 奎宁成为治疗疟疾的特效药。
senses.why: Old pharmacy used the noun specific for a remedy aimed at exactly one ailment.
senses.whyCN: 旧时药房用名词 specific 指专治某一种病的特效药。

senses.title: A precise detail
senses.definition: a precise item of information, usually in the plural specifics
senses.definitionCN: 一条精确的信息，常用复数 specifics
senses.example: The contract still lacks the specifics of payment.
senses.exampleCN: 合同仍缺少付款的具体细节。
senses.why: Turn the adjective into a noun and you hold the magnified details in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 把形容词变成名词，被放大的细节就握在手中。

senses.title: In biology: limited to one species
senses.definition: restricted to or characteristic of one biological species
senses.definitionCN: 仅限于或专属于某一生物物种
senses.example: The virus shows strong species-specific behaviour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒表现出很强的物种特异性。
senses.why: The exactness of the lens becomes biological: it fits one living kind only.
senses.whyCN: 镜头的精确性变成生物学概念：它只匹配一种生物。

senses.title: Made definite by naming
senses.definition: made definite by naming the very thing intended
senses.definitionCN: 通过指明确切对象而变得确定
senses.example: The winner was made specific once the envelope opened.
senses.exampleCN: 信封一开，获奖者就确定了。
senses.why: Naming is the final act of precision: the one thing is finally spoken.
senses.whyCN: 指名是精确的最终动作：那唯一的事物终于被说出。

intro.en: Specific comes from Latin via Late Latin and Old French, and its family is all about naming a kind exactly.
intro.cn: specific 经晚期拉丁语和古法语来自拉丁语，其词族的核心是精确地指明一个种类。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Species meant "a kind, appearance", from specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「种类、外貌」，由 specere「看」派生。

items.en: Late Latin specificus meant "constituting a kind of its own", used in philosophical and medical texts.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 specificus 意为「自成一种的」，用于哲学与医学文本。

items.en: Medieval physicians used specific remedies aimed at one disease, giving the word its medical sense.
items.cn: 中世纪医师使用针对单一疾病的 specific 药物，赋予该词医学义项。

items.en: The word entered English in the seventeenth century with both the logical and the medical senses.
items.cn: 该词于十七世纪进入英语，兼具逻辑义与医学义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same seeing-and-naming family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for the exact and the particular.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「观看—指名」词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示精确、特定的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning clearly or especially; built directly from specific.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「明确地；特别地」，由 specific 直接构成。

entries.definition: A written statement of exact details or requirements.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规格、说明书」，写明确切细节。

entries.definition: A sample taken for study; from the same Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，出自同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The quality of being precise or unique to a target.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「明确性、特异性」。

entries.definition: A baby's dummy or something that calms; merely looks similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「安抚奶嘴、安抚者」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Fully correct and precise in every detail; stronger than specific.
entries.definitionCN: 在每个细节上都完全正确精确，比 specific 更强。

entries.definition: Referring to one individual case out of many.
entries.definitionCN: 指众多之中某一单独的情形。

entries.definition: Carefully exact in measurement or statement.
entries.definitionCN: 在度量或表述上仔细而精确。

entries.definition: Clearly fixed and not likely to change.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚确定、不易改变的。

entries.definition: Stated openly and clearly, leaving nothing implied.
entries.definitionCN: 公开清楚地陈述，不留任何含蓄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and common phrases containing the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及包含该词的常见搭配。

normal.en: specere is to look: to be specific is to look closely enough to name one thing.
normal.cn: specere 意为「看」：做到 specific 就是看得足够近，从而指名一个事物。

normal.en: The same family gives specify, specifically and specification.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 specify、specifically、specification。

normal.en: Be specific about the details, not about vague hopes.
normal.cn: 对细节要明确，不要停留在模糊的期望上。

normal.en: A remedy once called specific aims at exactly one disease.
normal.cn: 昔日称为 specific 的药专治一种病。

normal.en: Specific to means belonging only to that one thing.
normal.cn: specific to 表示只属于那一个事物。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a printed page: one word swells while the rest blur.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜压在书页上：一个词变大，其余模糊。

abstract.en: Being specific is like aiming a flashlight: the beam covers one target only.
abstract.cn: 做到 specific 就像打手电：光束只罩住一个目标。

abstract.en: Vague answers scatter like sand; specific answers click into one slot.
abstract.cn: 模糊的回答像散沙，具体的回答咔哒落入唯一的槽。

examples.en: She asked for specific instructions on assembling the shelf.
examples.cn: 她要求给出组装书架的具体说明。

examples.en: The allergy is specific to peanuts and tree nuts.
examples.cn: 这种过敏只针对花生和坚果。

examples.en: Can you be more specific about which files were deleted?
examples.cn: 关于删除了哪些文件，你能说得更具体些吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西菲克」——锁定一种而不及其他：明确的；特定的

root: 晚期拉丁语 specificus「自成一种的」由 species「种类」+ 后缀 -ficus「做成的」构成，species 又来自 specere「观看」；更早的印欧词根 *spek-「观察」一般认为成立，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of specific all narrow a field to one point: exact in statement, tied to one target, or holding the details themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: specific 的各项义项都把范围收窄到一点：表述精确、针对单一对象，或本身就承载细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass that lights exactly one point out of a page of possibilities.
core.cn: 核心意象：放大镜在满页可能中照亮唯一的一点。

branches.en: THE CLARITY LINE: a statement becomes usable when it is exact and detailed.
branches.cn: 清晰线：表述精确而详实时才可使用。

branches.en: THE TARGETING LINE: the word picks one case or one species out of many.
branches.cn: 瞄准线：这个词从众多中挑出一个情形或一个物种。

branches.en: THE BELONGING LINE: what is specific to a thing belongs to it alone.
branches.cn: 归属线：特有之物只属于那个事物。

branches.en: THE OLD MEDICINE LINE: the pharmacy sense keeps the one-target image alive.
branches.cn: 旧药学线：药房义项保留单目标意象。

branches.en: THE HELD-DETAILS LINE: the noun specifics and the act of naming carry the magnified point.
branches.cn: 细节线：名词 specifics 与指名的动作承载被放大的那一点。

intro.en: Specific is built on the Latin kind-word species plus a making suffix; English keeps adding the usual extensions.
intro.cn: specific 建立在拉丁「种类」词 species 之上并加「做成」后缀；英语在其上继续常规扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin species, specere and Late Latin specificus are recorded; the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species、specere 与晚期拉丁语 specificus 均有记录，印欧词根为重构形式。

definition_zh: 接近；靠近；临近；方法；途径；处理；对付；通路；入口
definition_en: to come near a place, person, or time; a way of dealing with something; or the path that leads to a place
core_image: 脚步一步步靠近一扇门，手里还带着一套办法
scene: 山路上，两个人迎着晨雾向村子走去。 As they approached the village, the church bell began to ring.
sceneCN: 这里 approach 是「接近；靠近」（第 1 个义项：在空间上向某处移动、靠近）；句意为「他们走近村子时，教堂的钟开始响」。画面里有蜿蜒的山路、晨雾与远处的村庄。

pos.zh: 动词：接近；靠近；临近；处理；对付
名词：方法；途径；通路；入口

senses.title: To move nearer
senses.definition: to move nearer to a place, person, or object
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上向某地、某人或某物移动得更近
senses.example: As they approached the village, the church bell began to ring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走近村子时，教堂的钟开始响。
senses.why: Late Latin appropiare joined ad- 'to' with prope 'near'; the verb is simply the act of getting nearer.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appropiare 把 ad-「向」与 prope「近」连起来；这个动词就是变得更近的动作。

senses.title: A way of dealing with something
senses.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or of doing a task
senses.definitionCN: 处理问题或完成任务的某种方式
senses.example: The teacher tried a different approach to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 老师尝试了一种不同的阅读教学法。
senses.why: A path that leads to a place becomes a path that leads to a solution.
senses.whyCN: 通向一个地点的路径，变成了通向一个解法的路径。

senses.title: To begin dealing with
senses.definition: to begin to deal with a problem, task, or person in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式开始处理问题、任务或某人
senses.example: We need to approach the question from the data.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要从数据出发来处理这个问题。
senses.why: Coming near a problem is the first step of handling it.
senses.whyCN: 靠近一个问题，就是处理它的第一步。

senses.title: To come close in time
senses.definition: to come close in time, as a season, event, or deadline
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上临近，如季节、事件或截止日期
senses.example: As winter approaches, the nights grow longer.
senses.exampleCN: 随着冬天临近，夜变得更长。
senses.why: The space word is applied to the calendar: a season also draws near.
senses.whyCN: 空间词被用到日历上：一个季节也会逐渐靠近。

senses.title: The road that leads in
senses.definition: the road, path, or way by which one reaches a place
senses.definitionCN: 抵达某处所经的道路、路径或通道
senses.example: The approach to the castle was steep and narrow.
senses.exampleCN: 通往城堡的路又陡又窄。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical path that the verb travels along.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留的正是动词所走的那条实体路径。

intro.en: Approach comes from the Latin words for 'near', and it moves easily from space to time to method.
intro.cn: approach 来自拉丁语中表示「近」的词，并从空间自然滑向时间与方法。

items.en: Prope means 'near', and it supplies the whole family with its idea of closeness.
items.cn: prope 意为「近」，它为整族词提供了「接近」的观念。

items.en: Ad- plus prope formed appropiare, 'to come near to'.
items.cn: ad- 与 prope 构成 appropiare，意为「靠近」。

items.en: French aprochier carries the verb into English with the same physical sense.
items.cn: 法语 aprochier 把这个动词带进英语，仍保留同样的空间义。

items.en: English approchen appears in the fourteenth century; the noun follows soon after.
items.cn: 英语 approchen 在十四世纪出现，名词紧随其后。

items.en: The word extends from walking nearer to the method one takes toward a problem.
items.cn: 这个词从走近某处扩展到面对问题时采取的方法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the approach family and a near-spelling trap; the near-meaning group gathers words for method and access.
note.cn: 形近组收 approach 的词族与一个拼写陷阱；近义组收表示方法与通道的词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗奇」——脚步一步一步靠近那扇门：接近；方法

root: approach 经古法语 aprochier 来自晚期拉丁语 appropiare「靠近」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 prope「近」构成。这个词从空间的走近出发，逐步扩展：走近一个地方的那条路就是通路与入口；面对一个问题时走的那条路就是方法；季节与截止日期也会在时间上靠近；而开始处理一件事，本质上就是先靠近它。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses radiate from nearness: walking closer, a road in, a method, the start of handling, and a season drawing near.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从「近」辐射出去：走近、进去的路、方法、开始处理，以及季节临近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps on a road, closing the distance to a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：路上的脚步，一点点缩短与一扇门的距离。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE LINE: the body moves closer.
branches.cn: 距离线：身体向目标靠近。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: the road becomes a way of thinking.
branches.cn: 方法线：那条路变成一种思路。

branches.en: THE HANDLING LINE: coming close is the first move.
branches.cn: 处理线：靠近就是第一个动作。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: a season closes the distance in time.
branches.cn: 日历线：季节在时间上缩短距离。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: the noun names the path itself.
branches.cn: 道路线：名词命名那条路本身。

intro.en: Approach is a French-shaped Latin verb, and its suffixes are all productive in English.
intro.cn: approach 是一个法语外形的拉丁动词，它的后缀在英语里都还能产词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is prope 'near', visible inside appropiare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 prope「近」，它就在 appropiare 里面。

items.meaning: to come near or to begin handling
items.example: The train approached the station slowly.
The new teacher is very approachable.

items.meaning: the quality of being easy to meet
items.example: Her approachability won the team over.
They prepared for the approaching storm.
items.exampleCN: 他们为即将到来的暴风雨做准备。

items.meaning: a road leading to a place
items.example: The approach road was closed for repairs.
items.exampleCN: 通往那里的路因维修关闭。

items.example: They agreed on a new approach to teaching.
items.exampleCN: 他们商定了一种新的教学法。

items.example: The report calls for a new approach.

definition_zh: 共和国；共和政体
definition_en: a country governed by elected representatives and a president rather than a king or queen
core_image: 广场上的人群把王冠收进箱子，换上写着「公共事务」的旗帜
scene: 国王退位后，议会宣布国家改为共和国，权力归全体公民。 The country became a republic after the revolution.
sceneCN: 这里 republic 是「共和国」（第 1 个义项：由选举产生的代表治理、不设君主的国家）；句意：革命之后，这个国家成为共和国。

derivatives.zh: 共和主义者
共和主义

senses.title: Government by elected representatives
senses.definition: a form of government in which power belongs to elected representatives and a president, not a monarch
senses.definitionCN: 权力属于民选代表和总统、而非君主的一种政体
senses.example: The thinkers argued for a republic based on law.
senses.exampleCN: 这些思想家主张建立以法律为基础的共和政体。
senses.why: The Latin phrase res publica means the public thing, so the core sense is government as a shared public matter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁短语 res publica 意为「公共之事」，所以核心义是把治理视为公共事务。

senses.title: A country with that government
senses.definition: a particular country whose head of state is a president rather than a king
senses.definitionCN: 元首是总统而不是国王的某个具体国家
senses.example: France is a republic with a powerful president.
senses.exampleCN: 法国是一个总统权力很大的共和国。
senses.why: The abstract system gives its name to the concrete state that adopts it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的制度把名称给了采用它的具体国家。

senses.title: The commonwealth of citizens
senses.definition: the whole body of citizens considered as a public community
senses.definitionCN: 被视为公共共同体的全体公民
senses.example: In classical thought the republic includes every citizen.
senses.exampleCN: 在古典思想中，共和国包含每一位公民。
senses.why: This older sense keeps the literal meaning of res publica, the public affair shared by all.
senses.whyCN: 这个较古老的义项保留了 res publica 的字面意思：由所有人共享的公共事务。

intro.en: Republic comes from Latin res publica, the public thing or public affair, through French république.
intro.cn: republic 来自拉丁语 res publica（公共之事），经法语 république 进入英语。

items.en: Res means a thing or matter, and publica means public or belonging to the people.
items.cn: res 意为事物、事情，publica 意为公共的、属于人民的。

items.en: Res publica names the state as a shared public concern rather than a ruler's property.
items.cn: res publica 把国家称为公共关切，而不是统治者的私产。

items.en: Roman writers use res publica for the commonwealth and its constitution.
items.cn: 罗马作家用 res publica 指共和国体及其宪制。

items.en: Old French republique shortens the phrase into a single noun.
items.cn: 古法语 republique 把这一短语压缩成一个名词。

items.en: Middle English republic names a state without a monarch.
items.cn: 中古英语 republic 指不设君主的国家。

items.en: Modern English uses republic for both the system and the country.
items.cn: 现代英语中，republic 既指制度，也指国家。

note.en: Republic is a public-thing word, and its family includes the supporter and the doctrine, while it sits near other names for states.
note.cn: republic 是一个「公共之事」的词，其词族包括支持者与主义，同时与其它国家名称相邻。

entries.definition: a supporter of republican government
entries.definitionCN: 共和主义者

entries.definition: the belief in government by elected representatives
entries.definitionCN: 共和主义

entries.definition: government in which people choose their leaders
entries.definitionCN: 民主；民主制度

entries.definition: a state or community founded for the common good
entries.definitionCN: 共和国；联邦

entries.definition: an organized political community under one government
entries.definitionCN: 国家；州

entries.definition: a large group of people sharing a country or identity
entries.definitionCN: 民族；国家

normalIntro.en: Republic contains public, and the deeper story is res publica, the public thing, so the memory hook is government treated as public property.
normalIntro.cn: republic 含有 public，更深的故事是 res publica（公共之事），记忆钩子是「把治理当作公共财产」。

normal.en: See public inside republic: the public thing belongs to the citizens.
normal.cn: 在 republic 里看到 public：公共之事属于公民。

normal.en: A republic has a president instead of a king.
normal.cn: 共和国由总统而不是国王担任元首。

normal.en: The Republic of Ireland is a country name that uses the word directly.
normal.cn: the Republic of Ireland 是直接使用这个词的国家名称。

normal.en: Declare a republic is what a revolution often does.
normal.cn: declare a republic 常是革命之后的动作。

normal.en: Compare republican: the ending -an marks a supporter or an adjective.
normal.cn: 对比 republican：词尾 -an 标记支持者或形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a crown being placed in a wooden box and the lid shut.
abstract.cn: 想象王冠被放进木箱，箱盖合上。

abstract.en: Imagine a flag with the words public business on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一面写着「公共事务」的旗帜。

abstract.en: Think of a town square where citizens vote under open sky.
abstract.cn: 想象市民在露天广场上投票。

examples.en: The country declared itself a republic in the last century.
examples.cn: 这个国家在上个世纪宣布成为共和国。

examples.en: The republic elects a president every five years.
examples.cn: 这个共和国每五年选举一次总统。

examples.en: Ancient writers debated the best form of a republic.
examples.cn: 古代作家讨论过最好的共和政体形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: re + public：公共之事归公众，即共和国；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）+ publica（公共的）→ res publica（公共之事）→ 古法语 republique → 中古英语 republic，指由民选代表治理、不设君主的国家。

sensesIntro.en: The public thing comes first as a system, then as a particular country, and finally as the whole community of citizens.
sensesIntro.cn: 「公共之事」先是作为一种制度，再成为具体的国家，最后指全体公民构成的共同体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: government treated as a public possession rather than a royal estate.
core.cn: 核心意象：治理被当作公共财产，而不是王室的私产。

branches.en: The system of elected government is the core political sense.
branches.cn: 民选代表的治理制度，是核心政治义项。

branches.en: The system gives its name to the country that adopts it.
branches.cn: 制度把名称给了采用它的国家。

branches.en: The oldest sense keeps the whole citizen body in view.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项保留了全体公民这一整体。

branches.en: System and state are two levels of the same public arrangement.
branches.cn: 制度与国家是同一公共安排的两个层次。

branches.en: A country and its citizens are the container and the community inside it.
branches.cn: 国家是容器，公民是其中的共同体。

intro.en: Republic is a Latin phrase compressed into an English noun, so its parts are words rather than prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: republic 是由拉丁短语压缩成的英语名词，其成分是词而不是前后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin res publica means the public thing, and English keeps the idea while borrowing the French form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res publica 意为「公共之事」，英语借用法语形式并保留这一观念。

items.example: Res appears in the Latin phrase res publica.
items.exampleCN: res 出现在拉丁短语 res publica 中。

items.example: Publica qualifies res in res publica.
items.exampleCN: publica 在 res publica 中修饰 res。

items.example: Res publica is the direct source of republic.
items.exampleCN: res publica 是 republic 的直接来源。

items.example: Old French republique shortens the Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 republique 压缩了这一拉丁短语。

items.meaning: relating to or a person of

definition_zh: 遥远的；偏僻的；疏远的；微小的；远程的
definition_en: far away in distance or time, or not closely connected
core_image: 一条土路通向山后，远处的房子小得只剩一个点
scene: 那里没有公交，最近的诊所也在两个小时车程之外。 There is no bus service, and the nearest clinic is two hours away in a remote valley.
sceneCN: 这里 remote 是「偏僻的、遥远的」（第 1 个义项：距离很远）；句意：那里没有公交，最近的诊所位于两个小时车程之外的偏僻山谷。

pos.zh: 遥远的；偏僻的；疏远的；微小的；远程的

derivatives.zh: remote 加 -ly 构成，义为「遥远地；丝毫（用于否定）」
remote 加 -ness 构成，义为「遥远；偏僻」
与 remote 同出拉丁语 removere，义为「移开；去除」

senses.title: Far away in space or time
senses.definition: a long way from towns, people, or the present time
senses.definitionCN: 距离城镇、人群或当下时间很远
senses.example: They live in a remote village in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在山中的偏远村庄里。
senses.why: The Latin participle remotus means moved back, so the core image is something pushed to a distance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词 remotus 意为「被移开的」，所以核心画面是被推到远处的某个东西。

senses.title: Distant in manner
senses.definition: not friendly or close, keeping other people at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 不亲近，把他人挡在一定的距离之外
senses.example: His manner was polite but remote.
senses.exampleCN: 他的态度礼貌，却显得疏远。
senses.why: If something can be moved far away in space, a person can also hold others far away in feeling.
senses.whyCN: 既然东西可以在空间上被推远，人也可以在情感上把别人挡在远处。

senses.title: Very slight or unlikely
senses.definition: existing only in a small amount, so that it is unlikely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 只存在很小的一点，因此不太可能发生
senses.example: There is only a remote possibility of rain this week.
senses.exampleCN: 这周下雨的可能性很小。
senses.why: Distance in space turns into distance in probability: what is far off is unlikely to arrive.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的距离会变成概率上的距离：离得远的东西，就很难真的到来。

senses.title: Operated from a distance
senses.definition: controlled or done from a place that is not the place of action
senses.definitionCN: 在非现场的位置进行控制或操作
senses.example: She works from a remote office two hundred miles away.
senses.exampleCN: 她在两百英里外的远程办公点工作。
senses.why: The plain idea of being far away gives the modern technical sense of working or controlling at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 「处在远处」这个朴素含义，给出了现代远程工作与远程控制的技术义。

intro.en: Remote is the past participle of Latin removere, to move back, which also gives the verb remove.
intro.cn: remote 是拉丁语 removere「移开」的过去分词，同一个动词也产生了 remove。

items.en: Removere joins re- with movere, to move, and means to move back or away.
items.cn: removere 由 re- 与 movere「移动」组合，意为向后移开或移走。

items.en: The participle remotus describes something that has been moved away, hence distant.
items.cn: 分词 remotus 描述被移走的东西，因而表示遥远。

items.en: Movere also gives motion, motive, and mobile, all about movement.
items.cn: movere 还产生 motion、motive、mobile 等词，都与移动有关。

items.en: English remote first means far off in space or time.
items.cn: 英语 remote 最初表示在空间或时间上遥远。

items.en: The word widens to cover an aloof manner, a slight chance, and work done at a distance.
items.cn: 词义扩展到冷淡的态度、微小的可能性以及在远处完成的工作。

note.en: Remote shares its Latin verb with remove, and it stands beside words for distance and for aloofness.
note.cn: remote 与 remove 共享同一个拉丁动词，并与表示距离和冷淡的词相邻。

entries.definition: from a distance, or by even a small amount
entries.definitionCN: 远程地；丝毫（多用于否定），由 remote 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: to take something away
entries.definitionCN: 移开；去除，与 remote 同出拉丁语 removere

entries.definition: the act of moving
entries.definitionCN: 运动；动作，与 remote 共享 movere 词根

entries.definition: far away in space or time
entries.definitionCN: 遥远的，是最直接的近义词

entries.definition: far from other places or people
entries.definitionCN: 孤立的；偏僻的，强调与外界隔绝

entries.definition: not friendly and deliberately distant
entries.definitionCN: 冷淡的；疏远的，与第二义项接近

normalIntro.en: Remote and remove are twins from the Latin verb removere, so distance and removal sit side by side.
normalIntro.cn: remote 与 remove 是拉丁动词 removere 的双生词，距离与移开因此相邻。

normal.en: Re- plus movere, to move, gives something moved away and therefore far off.
normal.cn: 前缀 re- 加 movere「移动」，就是被移走因而很远的。

normal.en: Remove is the verb, remote the adjective, and remoteness the noun.
normal.cn: remove 是动词，remote 是形容词，remoteness 是名词。

normal.en: The movere root also drives motion, motive, and mobile.
normal.cn: movere 词根也驱动着 motion、motive 与 mobile。

normal.en: Remote control and remote access are the two modern fixed phrases.
normal.cn: remote control 与 remote access 是两个现代固定说法。

normal.en: In the negative, remotely means at all, as in not remotely ready.
normal.cn: 在否定句中，remotely 表示「丝毫」，如 not remotely ready。

abstract.en: Picture a single light on a hillside hours away from the road.
abstract.cn: 想象山坡上一点孤灯，离公路还有几个小时。

abstract.en: See a person answering politely while stepping half a pace back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人礼貌回答，同时后退半步。

abstract.en: Think of a hand controller working a machine in another room.
abstract.cn: 想一只遥控器在另一个房间操纵机器。

examples.en: The farm is remote and hard to reach in winter.
examples.cn: 这个农场很偏僻，冬天很难到达。

examples.en: There is a remote chance that the letter survived.
examples.cn: 那封信还有极小的可能保存下来。

examples.en: He seemed remote and said almost nothing.
examples.cn: 他显得疏远，几乎什么也没说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞摩托」——想象骑着摩托在瑞丽山里越走越远；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 remotus，是 removere（re-「向后」+ movere「移动」）的过去分词，字面即「被移远的」。

sensesIntro.en: Being moved far away gives physical distance, emotional distance, small probability, and distance in control.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被移远」既给出物理距离，也给出情感距离、微小的可能性，以及控制上的距离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house shrunk to a dot beyond the hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：山那边的房子缩成了一个小点。

branches.en: Physical distance is the base of every other sense.
branches.cn: 物理距离是其他所有义项的基础。

branches.en: Distance in feeling produces the aloof manner.
branches.cn: 情感上的距离产生冷淡的态度。

branches.en: Distance in probability makes a chance remote.
branches.cn: 可能性上的距离使机会变得渺茫。

branches.en: Distance in control gives work and access at a distance.
branches.cn: 控制上的距离产生远程工作与远程访问。

branches.en: All three are the same refusal to be close.
branches.cn: 三者都是同一种「不愿靠近」。

intro.en: Remote is a Latin particle frozen into an English adjective, carrying a prefix and a movement root.
intro.cn: remote 是凝固成英语形容词的拉丁分词，带着前缀与表示移动的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back, and movere means to move, so remotus means moved back or away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 表示「向后」，movere 表示「移动」，因此 remotus 就是「被移开的」。

items.example: Re- gives the direction of the move.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 给出移动的方向。

items.example: The mov- root returns in motion and remove.
items.exampleCN: mov- 词根出现在 motion 与 remove 中。

items.example: Movere is the verb behind the root.
items.exampleCN: movere 是这个词根背后的动词。

items.example: The ending -tus makes remotus a participle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tus 使 remotus 成为分词。

items.example: Remotus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: remotus 是这个英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Remoteness names the quality of being far away.
Remove is the verb of the same Latin family.
items.exampleCN: remove 是同一拉丁词族的动词。

definition_zh: 轰鸣声；繁荣；迅速增长
definition_en: a deep loud sound that carries a long way
core_image: 山谷里滚过的一记闷雷
scene: 远处传来一声低沉的轰响。 A deep boom came from the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 boom 是「轰鸣声」（第 1 个义项：低沉而传得很远的响声）；句意是山里传来一声低沉的轰响。

pos.zh: 动词：发出轰响；迅速发展

derivatives.zh: 生育高峰期出生的人
短暂的小繁荣

senses.title: A deep loud sound
senses.definition: a deep hollow sound that travels far
senses.definitionCN: 低沉空洞、传得很远的响声
senses.example: A deep boom came from the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山里传来一声低沉的轰响。
senses.why: The word began as an imitation of this very sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是模仿这种声音。

senses.title: A period of fast growth
senses.definition: a time when business and trade grow quickly
senses.definitionCN: 商业与贸易迅速增长的时期
senses.example: The city enjoyed an economic boom.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市经历了经济繁荣。
senses.why: A growing economy was said to boom, like a loud swelling noise.
senses.whyCN: 经济增长被形容为 boom，像一阵越来越响的声音。

senses.title: To grow quickly
senses.definition: to increase or succeed very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 迅速增长或兴旺
senses.example: Sales boomed after the advertisement.
senses.exampleCN: 广告播出后销量猛增。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for anything rising fast.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指任何快速上升的事物。

intro.en: Boom copies a hollow sound, and the noise became a picture of fast growth.
intro.cn: boom 模仿空洞的响声，这种声音又成了快速增长的比喻。

items.en: the word copied a deep hollow noise.
items.cn: 这个词模仿低沉空洞的响声。

items.en: boom named the sound of cannon and thunder.
items.cn: boom 指大炮与雷的声音。

items.en: an economic boom described rapid growth.
items.cn: economic boom 形容迅速的经济增长。

items.en: baby boom named a sharp rise in births.
items.cn: baby boom 指出生率的骤增。

items.en: boom covers loud sound and fast growth.
items.cn: 如今 boom 兼指巨响与快速增长。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -oom ending; the near-meaning group names loud sounds and surges.
note.cn: 形近组共有 -oom 结尾；近义组是巨响与激增。

entries.definition: a flower on a plant
entries.definitionCN: 花朵

entries.definition: a brush with a long handle

definition_zh: 全体员工；人事部门；（军队或机构的）人员；某类专业人员
definition_en: the people who work for an organization, or the department that manages them; also the members of a force or of a particular group of workers
core_image: 一整面挂满名牌的墙，每块名牌后面都有一个正在上班的人
scene: 清晨的办公楼里，打卡机一声声响起，走廊尽头的人事办公室门口已经排起了队。 The personnel files were moved to the third floor last week.
sceneCN: 这里 personnel 指「人事部门」（第 2 个义项：管理员工档案与招聘的部门）；句意为上周人事档案被搬到了三层。图中可辨识物件：打卡机、走廊、写着「人事」的门牌。

pos.zh: 全体员工；人事部门；人员

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）而来，义为「人；个人」
由 person 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「个人的；私人的」
由 personal 加 -ity 构成，义为「个性；人格」
由 personal 加 -ly 构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」

senses.title: All the people who work for an organization
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a company, school, or other organization, considered as one group
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于公司、学校或其他机构的全体人员，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The company doubled its personnel within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在一年之内把员工人数翻了一倍。
senses.why: The word entered English as the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it named the persons attached to an organization before it named any office or list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词进入英语时，是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词直接当名词用，所以它先指「挂靠在一个机构下的那些人」，而不是先指某个办公室或名册。

senses.title: The department that hires staff and keeps their records
senses.definition: the office in an organization that deals with hiring, records, and the terms of employment
senses.definitionCN: 机构中负责招聘、档案与雇佣条件的部门
senses.example: She works in personnel at the head office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在总部的人事部门工作。
senses.why: Because personnel already meant the people themselves, the office that counts and files those people took the same name by metonymy, the container named after what it contains.
senses.whyCN: 既然 personnel 已经指人本身，负责清点、归档这些人的办公室就借用了同一个名字，这是以「所管之物」代指「管理机构」的转喻。

senses.title: The members of an armed force, counted as a body
senses.definition: the members of a military force or unit, especially when they are counted or listed
senses.definitionCN: 军队或部队的成员，尤指被清点、列入名册时
senses.example: The wounded personnel were flown out at night.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤人员夜间被空运撤离。
senses.why: Military paperwork treats soldiers as entries on a roll, so personnel in this sense means the names on the list rather than any single soldier.
senses.whyCN: 军队的文书把士兵当成名册上的一条记录，所以这个义项里的 personnel 指名单上的那些人，而不指某一个士兵。

senses.title: People of one particular kind working in an operation
senses.definition: the people of a specified profession or role who are present in a place or taking part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业或某一职责的人，出现在某个场所或参与某项行动
senses.example: Medical personnel arrived within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗人员在十分钟内赶到。
senses.why: The collective frame survives even when the group is defined by a profession, so personnel can attach to a type of worker rather than to a single employer.
senses.whyCN: 即使这群人是由职业来界定的，那个「集体」的框架依然保留，所以 personnel 可以挂在一类工作者身上，而不必依附于某一个雇主。

intro.en: Personnel is a French adjective that became a noun: it began as the personal and ended up meaning the persons.
intro.cn: personnel 本是法语里的一个形容词，后来转成名词：起点是「个人的」，终点是「那些人」。

items.en: Persona first meant a mask worn by an actor, then the role played, and finally the individual who plays it.
items.cn: persona 最初指演员戴的面具，接着指所扮演的角色，最后指扮演角色的那个人。

items.en: The adjective personalis was built on persona and meant belonging to a person.
items.cn: 形容词 personalis 由 persona 构成，意为「属于某个人的」。

items.en: Old French used personel for what belongs to one person, and this form reached English as personal.
items.cn: 古法语用 personel 表示「属于个人的」，这一形式进入英语后成为 personal。

items.en: French turned its adjective personnel into a noun for the staff of an office, and English borrowed that noun in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语把自己的形容词 personnel 转为名词，指一个机关的全班人员；英语在十九世纪初借来了这个名词。

items.en: English kept the French -el spelling, added the human-resources sense in the twentieth century, and still treats the word as a collective with no ordinary singular.
items.cn: 英语保留了法语 -el 的拼法，二十世纪又添上「人事部门」这一义项，并且至今把它当作集合名词，没有日常的单数形式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin persona through French and English; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who work somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语 persona 经法语到英语的线索排列；近义组收表示「在某处工作的人」的词。

entries.definition: Belonging to or concerning one particular person.

entries.definition: A team of people working together, especially on a ship or aircraft.

normalIntro.en: The word is a French adjective sitting in a noun's chair, and its whole family runs back to the Latin mask.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是坐在名词位置上的法语形容词，而它的整个词族都要回到拉丁语的「面具」那里。

normal.en: Personnel is the noun use of a French adjective meaning personal, so it names persons rather than things.
normal.cn: personnel 是法语中意为「个人的」那个形容词当名词用，所以它指人而不指物。

normal.en: The ending -el is French; English personal uses -al, and that one letter is the main reason the two words are so easily confused.
normal.cn: 词尾 -el 来自法语；英语的 personal 用 -al，这一个字母的差别正是两词极易混淆的主因。

normal.en: As a collective noun it normally takes no plural, and one worker is a member of the personnel, not a personnel.
normal.cn: 作为集合名词，它通常不加复数；单独一个人要说成「人员中的一员」，而不能直接说成一个人。

normal.en: Personnel department shortened to personnel is a metonymy: the office is named after the people it manages.
normal.cn: 把「人事部门」缩成 personnel 是转喻：办公室被按它所管理的人来命名。

normal.en: In military reports personnel is the count on the roll, so losses are reported as personnel losses rather than as individual names.
normal.cn: 在军事报告里，personnel 就是名册上的数目，所以损失按「人员损失」统计，而不逐个列名字。

abstract.en: Think of a wall of name tags: the word never points at one tag, only at the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一整面名牌墙：这个词从不指向某一块名牌，只指向整面墙。

abstract.en: A French adjective walked into English and sat down as a noun; the stress still falls on the last syllable, as in French.
abstract.cn: 一个法语形容词走进英语，坐下当了名词；重音至今落在最后一个音节上，和法语一样。

abstract.en: One word covers both the people and the office that counts them, because paperwork always follows people.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指人，也指清点人的办公室，因为文书总是跟在人后面。

examples.en: All personnel must show their badges at the gate.
examples.cn: 所有员工都必须在大门口出示工牌。

examples.en: She was transferred to personnel after five years on the shop floor.
examples.cn: 在车间干了五年之后，她被调到了人事部门。

examples.en: Additional medical personnel were sent to the region.
examples.cn: 更多医疗人员被派往该地区。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body of people attached to an organization; from that one collective sense grow the office that manages them, the roll of a military unit, and any named group of workers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是依附于某个机构的一群人；由这一个集合义长出管理他们的办公室、部队名册，以及任何被点名的一类专业工作者。
