definition_zh: 少数；少数派；少数群体；少数民族；未成年
definition_en: the smaller number or part of a group, a group that differs from most people, or the state of being below the legal age
core_image: 一大群白鸟里混着几只深色的鸟，深色的那几只格外显眼
scene: 礼堂里举手表决时，只有靠后排的几个人没有举手，显得有些孤单。 A minority of members opposed the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 minority 是「少数、少数票」（第 1 个义项：人数较少的那一部分）；句意为少数成员反对这项计划。画面里可抓住的物件：礼堂、举起的手、后排的几个人。

pos.zh: 少数；少数派；少数群体；少数民族；未成年

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁比较级 minor 直接借入，义为「较小的；次要的；未成年的」
由 minority 词干加 -arian 构成，义为「少数派的；少数派成员」
由 minority 与 owned 复合，义为「少数族裔拥有的」

senses.title: The smaller number in a group
senses.definition: the smaller part of a group, less than half of the people involved
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中人数较少的那一部分，即不到参与人数的一半
senses.example: Only a minority of shareholders backed the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数股东支持这次合并。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin minor, smaller, so the first sense simply compares two parts of a vote or a crowd and names the smaller one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 minor（较小的）之上，所以第一个义项只是把投票或人群分成两份，取其中较小的那一份。

senses.title: A group that differs from most people
senses.definition: a group of people who differ from the larger society in race, religion, language or culture
senses.definitionCN: 在种族、宗教、语言或文化上与更大的社会群体不同的一群人
senses.example: The school teaches in the languages of several minorities.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校用几种少数民族的语言授课。
senses.why: Once the smaller part is made of people with a shared identity, the comparative word becomes a social label for communities outside the majority.
senses.whyCN: 当那较小的一部分是由具有共同身份的人组成时，这个比较词就变成社会标签，用来指多数群体之外的社群。

senses.title: The state of being under legal age
senses.definition: the period during which a person is legally too young to manage their own affairs
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在法定上年纪尚小、不能自行处理事务的那段时期
senses.example: He inherited the estate while still in his minority.
senses.exampleCN: 他还在未成年时便继承了这份产业。
senses.why: Latin minor also meant younger, and the law borrowed the comparison to mark who is less than the age of full legal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minor 也有「较年轻」的意思，法律借用了这个比较，用来标出未达到完全法定年龄的人。

intro.en: Minority comes from Latin minor, smaller or younger, and reached English through French; its senses follow both comparisons, the smaller part and the younger person.
intro.cn: minority 来自拉丁语 minor（较小的、较年轻的），经法语进入英语；它的义项沿着两种比较展开：较少的部分与较年轻的人。

items.en: Minor was the comparative of parvus, meaning smaller, lesser or younger, and it is the stem behind the whole family.
items.cn: minor 是 parvus 的比较级，意为较小、较低或较年轻，是整族词的词干。

items.en: The abstract noun minoritas was formed with -itas to name the state of being smaller or younger.
items.cn: 抽象名词 minoritas 由 -itas 构成，用来指「较小」或「较年轻」的状态。

items.en: French used minorité for both the smaller part and the years before adulthood, and this form generally reached English.
items.cn: 法语用 minorité 兼指较少的部分与成年之前的年月，一般认为英语接收的正是这个形式。

items.en: English minority first named the state of being under age, and the sense of a smaller number followed.
items.cn: 英语中 minority 最早指未成年的状态，随后才出现「人数较少」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses and adds the social sense of an ethnic or religious minority.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这两个义项，并增加了「民族或宗教上的少数群体」这一社会义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin comparison of small; the near-meaning group collects words for a small part, a faction and the years before adulthood.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁「小」的比较系列上的词；近义组收表示小部分、派系与成年之前年岁的词。

entries.definition: Smaller, less important, or below the legal age of adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的、较次要的，或未达法定成年年龄的。

entries.definition: The mathematical sign for subtraction, or a state of being without something.
entries.definitionCN: 数学中的减号，或缺少某物的状态。

entries.definition: To become smaller or less in size, amount or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小、数量或重要性上变小或减少。

entries.definition: As small as possible; at the lowest end of a scale.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能小的；处在标度最低端的。

entries.definition: A very small number of people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 为数极少的人或物。

entries.definition: A small part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中很小的一部分。

entries.definition: A small organized group within a larger one, often in disagreement with it.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部一个有组织的小派别，常与主体意见不合。

entries.definition: Below the age at which the law treats a person as an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 低于法律视为成年人的年龄。

normalIntro.en: Minority is the state built on Latin minor, smaller or younger, and its family keeps measuring things against a larger other side.
normalIntro.cn: minority 建立在拉丁语 minor（较小、较年轻）之上的状态，它的一族词始终拿「更大的另一边」作参照。

normal.en: Minority is built on minor, Latin for smaller or younger, so the word carries a comparison before it carries any social meaning.
normal.cn: minority 建立在 minor（较小或较年轻）之上，所以这个词先带比较，再带社会含义。

normal.en: The -ity ending turns an adjective into a state or condition, just as major becomes majority.
normal.cn: -ity 词尾把形容词变成状态或性质，就像 major 变成 majority 一样。

normal.en: In the minority is the everyday frame: whoever is counted there is on the smaller side of a vote.
normal.cn: in the minority 是日常框架：被算在里面的人，就是投票中人数较少的一边。

normal.en: Ethnic minority and minority group show the word naming communities, not just numbers.
normal.cn: ethnic minority 与 minority group 展示了这个词如何命名社群，而不只是数字。

normal.en: The legal sense is the older one in English: minority first meant the years before a person reaches full age.
normal.cn: 法律义在英语里更早：minority 最初指一个人达到完全年龄之前的那些年。

abstract.en: Picture a flock of pale birds with a few darker ones among them: the dark birds are few but easy to see.
abstract.cn: 想象一大群浅色鸟里夹着几只深色的：深色的数量少，却很容易被看见。

abstract.en: A minority is a comparison turned into a group; the word always implies a larger other side.
abstract.cn: minority 是被变成群体的比较；这个词始终暗示着一个更大的对立面。

abstract.en: The same stem covers a voting count, a community and a child's years, because all three are measured as less than something else.
abstract.cn: 同一个词干覆盖投票计数、社群与童年，因为三者都是相对于某个更大对象而被量出来的「较少」。

examples.en: Only a minority of shareholders backed the merger.
examples.cn: 只有少数股东支持这次合并。

examples.en: The school teaches in the languages of several minorities.
examples.cn: 这所学校用几种少数民族的语言授课。

examples.en: He inherited the estate while still in his minority.
examples.cn: 他还在未成年时便继承了这份产业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买诺瑞提」——买票时数一数，多数一大把，少数就那么几张，提出来格外显眼；minority 是少数。

root: 拉丁语 minor（较小的、较年轻的）是 parvus（小）的比较级；抽象名词 minoritas 经法语 minorité 进入英语，一般认为先指未成年，后指少数。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the smaller side of a comparison; the senses run from a voting count to a social group and to the years before legal adulthood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是比较中较小的那一边；各义项从投票计数走到社会群体，再到法定成年之前的年岁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flock of pale birds with a few darker ones standing out among them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大群浅色鸟里，几只深色的格外显眼。

branches.en: a few hands raised against a crowded hall
branches.cn: 满堂之中只有几只举起的手

branches.en: a classroom where several home languages are spoken
branches.cn: 几种家庭语言同时存在的教室

branches.en: a young heir signing papers before coming of age
branches.cn: 未成年的继承人签下文件

branches.en: a small group that shares a name and a voice
branches.cn: 人数少却有共同名字与声音的一群人

branches.en: the same word measuring a community and a childhood
branches.cn: 同一个词既量社群也量童年

intro.en: Minority joins a Latin comparative of small to an abstract suffix, and its items show how a comparison becomes a social category.
intro.cn: minority 把拉丁语「小」的比较级接到抽象后缀上，各构词条目展示了比较如何变成社会类别。

latinIntro.en: Minority rests on the Latin comparative minor, smaller or younger, and the same stem appears in minor, minus and diminish.
latinIntro.cn: minority 建立在拉丁语比较级 minor（较小的、较年轻的）之上，同一词干见于 minor、minus 与 diminish。

definition_zh: 登记；注册；挂号；登记手续；登记记录
definition_en: the act or process of writing down one's name on an official list, or the certificate and record that result
core_image: 在一张官方名册上写下自己的名字：名字落进格子里，格子把它变成一份被承认的存在
scene: 大厅里排着长队，每个人手里都攥着表格和证件。 Registration for the new term closes on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 registration 是「注册；登记」（第 1 个义项：把名字写上官方名单的过程）；句意：新学期注册在周五截止。场景要点：排队的人群、表格、章印。

pos.zh: 登记；注册；挂号；登记手续；登记记录

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「登记；注册；（仪表）显示」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「登记者；注册人」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「登记处；登记簿；注册处」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「登记员；教务主任；（医院）主治医师助理」

senses.title: The act of putting a name on a list
senses.titleCN: 把名字写上名册的行为
senses.definition: the process of entering a name on an official list, as for school, a conference, or a course
senses.definitionCN: 把名字录入官方名单的过程，如入学、参会或选课
senses.example: Registration for the conference takes place in the main hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大会的登记在主厅进行。
senses.why: The Latin gesta means 'things carried out, written deeds': registration is the writing-down that makes you carried out and counted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 gesta 意为「已完成之事、写下的事迹」：registration 就是那份让你「被记录、被计入」的写下。

senses.title: Official recording of ownership or status
senses.titleCN: 所有权或身份的官方登记
senses.definition: the official recording of a fact such as who owns a car, land, or company, giving it legal force
senses.definitionCN: 对车辆、土地或公司的归属等事实的官方记录，使其具有法律效力
senses.example: The registration of the car must be renewed every year.
senses.exampleCN: 车辆的登记须每年更新。
senses.why: Writing the fact down gives it a body the law can hold: the record becomes the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 把事实写下来，就给了法律可以握住的实体：记录本身成了那件事物。

senses.title: The certificate or plate that proves it
senses.titleCN: 证明登记的证件或号牌
senses.definition: the document, number, or plate that shows an entry has been made, as car registration plates
senses.definitionCN: 显示已完成登记的文件、号码或号牌，如汽车登记号牌
senses.example: He checked the registration on the front of the van.
senses.exampleCN: 他核对了面包车前的登记号牌。
senses.why: The written deed is carried about in metal and paper: the record leaves the book and rides on the door.
senses.whyCN: 写下的事迹被带在金属和纸上：记录离开簿册，钉上了车门。

senses.title: The total number of people registered
senses.definition: the number of people or things that have been registered, as school registrations falling this year
senses.definitionCN: 已登记的人数或数量，如今年入学注册人数下降
senses.example: New registrations rose by a fifth last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月新增登记量增长了五分之一。
senses.why: The list, once full of names, can be counted: the act becomes a figure in a report.
senses.whyCN: 写满名字的名册可以被清点：行为变成了报告里的一个数字。

intro.en: Registration comes from register, from Latin regesta, past participle of regerere 'to carry back, record', from re- 'back' + gerere 'to carry, carry on, perform'. The register was first the book of things carried back and written down.
intro.cn: registration 来自 register，上溯拉丁语 regesta——regerere「带回、记录」的过去分词，由 re-「回」加 gerere「携带、进行、执行」构成。register 起初是「带回并写下之事」的簿册。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ghes- 'to carry, perform' underlies Latin gerere and its family geste, digest and suggestion.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *ghes-「携带、执行」生出拉丁语 gerere 及其家族 geste、digest、suggestion。

items.en: Regerere meant 'to carry back'; its plural noun regesta meant 'things recorded', the entries an official wrote down and kept.
items.cn: regerere 意为「带回」；其复数名词 regesta 意为「被记录之事」，即官员写下并保存的条目。

items.en: Medieval Latin registrum and Old French registre named the official book itself, kept in courts and chanceries.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 registrum 与古法语 registre 命名了那本官方簿册，存放于法庭与大法官署。

items.en: Register appears in English by the fourteenth century as the book of written entries; the verb follows soon after.
items.cn: register 十四世纪进入英语，指记录条目的簿册；动词很快跟上。

items.en: The action noun registration spreads with modern institutions: schools, elections, motor vehicles and online forms all hold their own lists.
items.cn: 行为名词 registration 随现代制度铺开：学校、选举、机动车与网上表格各有其名册。

note.en: The first group gathers the gerere 'carry out, record' family with its Latin endings. The second group compares the nouns of writing something down and being on a list.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 gerere「执行、记录」词族及其拉丁词尾。第二组比较「写下某事」与「列于名册」的名词。

entries.definition: to enter a name on a list, or the list and book itself. It is the root word.
entries.definitionCN: 把名字录入名册，或名册簿本本身。它是词根词。

entries.definition: the office or system that keeps official lists. It is where the writing-down lives.
entries.definitionCN: 保管官方名册的机构或系统。写下之事安家于此。

entries.definition: the official who keeps the register, at a school, court, or hospital.
entries.definitionCN: 保管名册的官员，见于学校、法院或医院。

entries.definition: the person whose name is written down. The passive member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名字被写下的人。词族中的被动一员。

entries.definition: to carry apart and sort out, hence to take apart food or information. Same carrying root, other direction.
entries.definitionCN: 分开搬运整理，引申为消化食物或信息。同一携带词根，方向不同。

entries.definition: the act of joining a school or course and being put on its roll. Enrolment is the joining; registration is the writing.
entries.definitionCN: 加入学校或课程并列入名册的行为。enrolment 重在加入；registration 重在记录。

entries.definition: the American spelling of enrolment, same meaning and same small l.
entries.definitionCN: enrolment 的美式拼写，词义相同。

entries.definition: the casual act of putting one's name down, especially online. It is registration without the office.
entries.definitionCN: 随意的报名，尤指网上。是没有官方机构在场的 registration。

entries.definition: a piece of information kept in writing or sound. Record stores what happened; registration admits you into a list.
entries.definitionCN: 以文字或声音保存的信息。record 储存事实；registration 把你写进名单。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin re- 'back' + gerere 'to carry, carry out', the family register, registrar, registry and digest, and the book-of-deeds picture.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 re-「回」加 gerere「携带、执行」，词族 register、registrar、registry、digest，以及「事迹簿」的图景。

normal.en: re- means back and gerere means carry out: the office carries your name back into its book.
normal.cn: re- 是「回」，gerere 是「执行」：办公室把你的名字带回它的簿册。

normal.en: Gesta, Roman deeds, came from the same verb: a register is a book of gesta.
normal.cn: 罗马人的「事迹」gesta 出自同一动词：register 就是一本事迹簿。

normal.en: The registrar is the person, the registry is the office, the registration is the act.
normal.cn: registrar 是人，registry 是机构，registration 是行为。

normal.en: Digest shares the root: your stomach and your mind both carry things apart to keep them.
normal.cn: digest 同根：胃和头脑都用「分开搬运」来保存事物。

normal.en: A number plate is registration made metal: the list rides on the car door.
normal.cn: 车牌是变成了金属的 registration：名册钉在车门上。

abstract.en: Picture one quiet desk, a ledger, and a pen: your name crossing onto the page is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张安静的桌子、一本账簿、一支笔：你的名字落上纸页，就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: Before registration you are a visitor; after it, a line in the book.
abstract.cn: 登记之前你是访客；登记之后，是簿册里的一行字。

abstract.en: Every queue at a desk is people waiting to become records.
abstract.cn: 每一支排队的长龙，都是等待变成记录的人。

examples.en: Bring two photos and your ID to the registration desk.
examples.cn: 请携带两张照片和证件到登记台。

examples.en: Early registration is cheaper than signing up on the day.
examples.cn: 提前注册比当天报名便宜。

examples.en: The land registration office confirmed the sale.
examples.cn: 土地登记处确认了这宗交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞记斯追神」——瑞福去登记，斯追着神官盖「记」章 → registration 登记；注册（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regesta「被记录之事」（regerere 带回记录：re- 回 + gerere 执行、携带），核心是「把名字或事实带回官方簿册、写成凭证」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of registration, all the same written deed: the act of entering the list, the legal record, the proof that travels, and the counted total.
sensesIntro.cn: registration 的四个义项是同一份「写下之事」：录入名册的行为、具有法律效力的记录、可以随行出示的凭证，以及被清点的总数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name crossing onto the page of an official book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字落上官方簿册的纸页。

branches.en: THE LIST: entering a name is one act; counting all the entries is the same act read in bulk.
branches.cn: 名册：录入一个名字是一次动作；清点所有条目是把同一动作按整体来读。

branches.en: THE LAW: once written down officially, ownership and status take on legal weight.
branches.cn: 法律：一旦正式写下，所有权与身份便有了法律分量。

branches.en: THE PROOF: plates and certificates carry the book's entry out into the street.
branches.cn: 凭证：号牌与证件把簿册里的条目带到了街上。

branches.en: ONE PEN, TWO POWERS: the same writing-down both admits you and secures your claim.
branches.cn: 一支笔，两种力量：同一次写下既接纳了你，也保全了你的权利。

branches.en: THE RECORD ABROAD: the proof travels and the numbers accumulate, both away from the original book.
branches.cn: 记录在途：凭证在流动，数字在累积，两者都已离开原来的簿册。

intro.en: Registration adds the Latin action suffix -ion to the stem gerere 'to carry, carry out' with the prefix re- 'back'. The gerere family also gives register, registrar, registry, digest and suggest.
intro.cn: registration 在词干 gerere「携带、执行」加前缀 re-「回」之上，附加拉丁行为后缀 -ion。gerere 词族还给出 register、registrar、registry、digest、suggest。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regerere 'to carry back' (re- 'back' + gerere 'to carry, perform'), whose plural noun regesta means 'things recorded'. Gerere is the same verb behind gesture and suggestion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regerere「带回」（re-「回」+ gerere「携带、执行」），其复数名词 regesta 意为「被记录之事」。gesture 与 suggestion 背后也是这个 gerere。

items.meaning: the act of entering on a list
items.meaningCN: 登记；注册（re- 回 + gerere 执行 + -ion 行为名词）

items.meaning: to enter on a list; the official book
items.meaningCN: 登记；名册（经中世纪拉丁语 registrum）
items.example: Register your name at the desk.

items.meaning: the official keeper of a register
items.meaningCN: 登记员；注册主任（-ar 表示官员）
items.example: Ask the registrar for a transcript.
items.exampleCN: 向注册主任要一份成绩单。

items.meaning: the office where lists are kept
items.meaningCN: 登记处；注册处（-y 表示场所）
登记者（-ant 表示被作用的人）
items.exampleCN: 每位登记者都拿到一枚胸牌。

items.meaning: to separate and take in; a summary
items.meaningCN: 消化；摘要（dis- 分开 + gerere 携带）
items.example: Give me a moment to digest the report.
items.exampleCN: 给我点时间消化这份报告。

items.meaning: to carry an idea under someone's mind; to hint
items.meaningCN: 暗示；建议（sub- 在下 + gerere 携带）
items.example: The data suggests an earlier date.

items.meaning: a movement of the body that carries meaning
items.meaningCN: 手势；姿态（-ure 构成名词）
items.example: A thumbs-up is a friendly gesture.
items.exampleCN: 竖起拇指是友好的手势。

items.meaning: to pile the story up beyond the truth
items.meaningCN: 夸大；言过其实（ex- 出 + 堆起）

items.meaning: the act of joining a school or course
items.meaningCN: 入学注册（英语本土词，与 registration 词源不同而义近）

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被记录之事；录下的条目

definition_zh: 石头；石料；果核；结石
definition_en: a hard piece of rock, rock used for building, or the hard seed of a fruit
core_image: 一块被溪水磨得光滑的灰色石头
scene: 孩子们在河边捡石头。 The children picked up stones by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 stone 是「石头」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们在河边捡石头。

derivatives.zh: 多石的；冷酷的
冷酷地
多石；冷酷

senses.title: A piece of rock
senses.definition: a hard solid piece of rock
senses.definitionCN: 一块坚硬的岩石
senses.example: The children picked up stones.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们捡起了石头。
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: Building rock
senses.definition: rock cut and used as a building material
senses.definitionCN: 切割后用作建筑材料的岩石
senses.example: The house is built of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 这房子是用石头建的。

definition_zh: 研究所；学院；建立；设立
definition_en: an organisation set up for research or teaching, or to set such a thing up
core_image: 几个人在空地上立起一块牌子，牌子围出一块新划定的地方
scene: 街角老楼前挂上了一块新铜牌，门厅里刚摆好桌椅。 The city decided to institute a new system for waste collection.
sceneCN: 这里 institute 是动词「设立、建立」（第 2 个义项：把制度或机构建立起来），句意是市政府决定设立新的垃圾收集制度。画面里能看到的物件：铜牌、桌椅、牌子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「机构；制度」
由 institution 加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已设立的」

senses.title: To set up a rule or system
senses.definition: to start a new rule, system, or practice and put it into effect
senses.definitionCN: 开始实行新的规则、制度或做法
senses.example: The council instituted a fine for late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会设立了逾期缴费罚款。
senses.why: Latin instituere means to set up; a rule is set up much as a building is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere 意为「设立」；规则被设立起来，就像建筑被立起来一样。

senses.title: An organisation for research
senses.definition: a body or building established for research, teaching, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为研究、教学或某种专业而建立的机构或场所
senses.example: She works at a small institute studying coastal life.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家研究海岸生物的小研究所工作。
senses.why: The thing set up became the institution itself: first a purpose, then the body that serves it.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来的东西变成了机构本身：先有一个目的，再有服务于它的组织。

senses.title: To begin a legal action
senses.definition: to start legal proceedings against someone, in formal usage
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中，对某人提起诉讼
senses.example: The company instituted proceedings against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起了诉讼。
senses.why: A case is formally set up before a court, so the same verb covers starting it.
senses.whyCN: 案件在法庭上被正式设立起来，所以同一动词也指「提起诉讼」。

intro.en: Institute comes from Latin instituere "to set up, place in position", built on statuere "to make stand".
intro.cn: institute 来自拉丁语 instituere「设立、安置」，基于 statuere「使之站立」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" and its causative statuere "to make stand, set up" are classical.
items.cn: stare「站立」及其使役形式 statuere「使站立、设立」都见于古典拉丁语。

items.en: In- plus statuere gave instituere, "to set up, undertake, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 statuere 得到 instituere，意为「设立、着手、教导」。

items.en: The noun institutum meant a purpose, a custom, or an arrangement.
items.cn: 名词 institutum 意为「目的、惯例、安排」。

items.en: Old French institut carried the noun into English as a name for a learned society.
items.cn: 古法语 institut 把名词传入英语，指学术团体。

items.en: From the eighteenth century institute names technical and research bodies.
items.cn: 自十八世纪起，institute 被用来命名技术与研究机构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root and the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for founding and organisations.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根与 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「设立」与「机构」的词。

entries.definition: An established organisation or custom, the noun of result.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度」，是结果名词。

entries.definition: To make up or form something, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「构成」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: To put one thing in place of another, with sub- meaning under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，前缀 sub- 表「在下」。

entries.definition: To set something up permanently, plainer than institute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建立」，比 institute 更朴素。

entries.definition: To be the first to start an organisation or city.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创建」，指最先发起组织或城市。

entries.definition: A learned society or school, a near synonym for the noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究院、学院」，与名词义近义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root and the double life of the word as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「站立」词根，以及这个词名词、动词两用的特点。

normal.en: in plus statuere: to set something standing, hence to set up.
normal.cn: in 加 statuere：让某物立起来，故为「设立」。

normal.en: Institute is both the act and the building.
normal.cn: institute 既是动作，也是建筑。

normal.en: A research institute institutes its own rules.
normal.cn: 研究所会设立自己的规矩。

normal.en: Same family as constitute and substitute.
normal.cn: 与 constitute、substitute 同族。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: Picture a sign being planted in empty ground.
abstract.cn: 想象在空地上立起一块牌子。

abstract.en: To institute is to give a habit a fixed address.
abstract.cn: 设立就是给一种习惯一个固定地址。

abstract.en: Institutions outlive the people who institute them.
abstract.cn: 机构比设立它的人活得更久。

examples.en: The school instituted a ban on phones in class.
examples.cn: 学校设立了课堂禁用手机的规定。

examples.en: He joined a research institute after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后他进入一家研究所。

examples.en: They instituted a new training programme.
examples.cn: 他们设立了一个新的培训项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是提土」——硬是提土来立招牌，就是设立机构

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ statuere「使站立、设立」→ in- + statuere = instituere「设立、着手」→ institutum「惯例、安排」→ 古法语 institut → 英语 institute。与 institution、constitute、substitute 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: setting up a rule, the research body itself, and starting legal action.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：设立规则、研究机构本身，以及提起诉讼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign is planted in empty ground and marks out a new place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块牌子被插进空地，划出一片新领域。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: a new rule is put in force.
branches.cn: 公告这条线：新规则被实行。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: a body created for research or teaching.
branches.cn: 建筑这条线：为研究或教学建立的机构。

branches.en: THE COURT: a case is formally begun.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式启动案件。

branches.en: THE LINK: every institute is itself instituted before it institutes anything.
branches.cn: 连接线：任何机构都要先被设立，才能设立别的。

branches.en: THE FORM: the legal sense belongs to a formal register.
branches.cn: 语域线：法律义属于正式语域。

intro.en: Institute is in- "in" plus the Latin statu- "set standing", with a participle ending.
intro.cn: institute 是 in-「入」加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再带分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin statuere, instituere and institutum are all recorded in classical and later texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 statuere、instituere、institutum 在古典及后世文献中均有记载。
